title: Patron of ecology (1979)
hookLine: John Paul II names Francis patron of those who care for creation

lines: A SONG FROM A SICK MAN.
cards: Brother Sun. Sister Moon and the stars. Brother Wind.
Sister Water. Brother Fire. It sounds like a roll call at a family reunion, and in a way it is.

These are the names Francis gives the world in a song in his own Italian dialect, the Canticle of the Creatures. Tradition says he made it near the end of his life, sick, his eyes so bad he could barely stand the light.
A man who could hardly see the sun called it his brother. Centuries later, a pope looked at that song and gave Francis a new job. Today's word is the job.

teach.h: A PATRON PRAYS FOR A PEOPLE OR A WORK.
teach.b: Pope John Paul II named Francis the patron of those who care for creation, the patron of ecology. A patron, for Catholics, is a saint in heaven asked to pray for a particular people or work.
So anyone who plants a tree has, in Catholic eyes, a friend in brown. Why Francis? Because of the Canticle.
It praises God for the sun, beautiful and radiant, who brings the day.

teach.h: SUN, WIND, WATER, FIRE: ALL PRAISE.
teach.b: For wind and air and every kind of weather. For water, useful and humble and precious and pure. For fire, bright and strong, who lights the night.
Then comes the surprise. Francis doesn't call the earth brother.

teach.h: EARTH: OUR SISTER AND OUR MOTHER.
teach.b: He calls her our sister and our mother, who feeds us and brings forth fruit and colored flowers and grass. Our line borrows the family word; the point is kinship. For Francis, creation isn't scenery.
It's family, all of it singing back to its maker. The Bible gives the job from the start.

teach.h: TO DRESS IT AND TO KEEP IT.
teach.b: In Genesis, in the Douay-Rheims, God puts the man in the garden "to dress it, and to keep it." To tend it and guard it, not to own it.

teach.h: ALL YE WORKS OF THE LORD, BLESS THE LORD.
teach.b: And the book of Daniel has a song inviting every creature in: "All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord." So a patron of ecology isn't a saint of recycling bins.
He's a saint who heard the world praying, and took his place in the choir.

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Francis in early October, and some parishes bless animals on or near that day; Catholic groups who work for the care of creation often take Francis as their patron.

games.q: you're Francis near the end of your life: sick, in pain, your eyes so weak you can barely stand the light. you have the strength to make one song. what is it?
o: a lament for everything you're losing.
praise of God for the sun, the water, the fire and the earth.
a list of rules for your brothers.
games.why: tradition says this is when he made the Canticle of the Creatures: a man who could hardly see the sun called it his brother.

practice: If you can step outside, walk a few steps, pick up three pieces of litter, a wrapper, a bottle cap, and carry them to a bin; if you can't go out, clear one small mess in the room you're in.
As you do, notice you're handling a small corner of the earth Francis called sister and mother, and if you pray, thank God for one creature you can see right now.

wordCard.voice: Patron of ecology. Francis, named by a pope as the saint who prays for those who care for creation, because he sang about the sun and the earth as family. Today's word.

orig.note: Francis's Umbrian dialect, in the Canticle: our sister, Mother Earth.

carryVoice: Your line: brother earth. Sun, water and earth, all one family. Same time tomorrow.
